correctness.rationale: Exact curvature -1 cusp-strip coordinates yield area densities w_i/H_i exp(-u)du. The distance of points in distinct cusps equals u+v+log(g_ij H_iH_j)+O_P(exp(-u)+exp(-v)); integrating the discrepancy band costs O_P(exp(-R)), and the exact Gamma(2,1) survival gives the leading R exp(-R) term. Same-cusp and core contributions are O_P(exp(-R)). Gauss-Bonnet normalizes by ((n-2)pi)^2. The quadrilateral coefficient simplifies to 2t^2/(pi^2(t-1)) with exact square extremizer. Direct checker tested the coordinate identity and numerical samples.

value.rationale: The natural uniform-pair geodesic-distance statistic on a finite-area, infinite-diameter ideal polygon has a cusp-pair long tail not captured by single-cusp behavior. The theorem resolves its exact leading shape-sensitive invariant for every fixed ideal n-gon, gives a nontrivial O(exp(-R)) remainder, and a unique sharp regular-quadrilateral extremizer. It is relevant to sampling and extreme pair distances in cusped geometric regions, not merely a renamed textbook identity.
